diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the exact manifold case when $q=0$, Theorem \ref{thmGeneralization} gives rise to the min-max regression error

issues.failure_explanation: The tube is defined with a strict inequality ||u|| < q*tau(v). For q=0 this requires ||u|| < 0, so M(0) is empty. The domain M(q) is then empty, no distribution P is supported on it, and f is defined nowhere. The paper nevertheless allows q in [0,1) and says q=0 recovers regression on the manifold itself and the minimax rate. As written, the definition does not cover that case.

failure_location.quote: When $q=0$, one recovers the exact manifold regression model

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a non-strict inequality ||u|| <= q*tau(v) for q=0, or restrict the theorems to q in (0,1) and treat q=0 separately (M(0)=M). The oracle construction and proofs go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised q=0 special case (exact manifold regression, minimax rate) is not covered by the stated definition and assumptions. Theorems 1 and 2 are vacuous at q=0. Results for q in (0,1) are unaffected.
issues.title: Tubular region is empty at q=0, so the exact-manifold/minimax claims are not covered as written
issues.why_classification: This is a one-symbol or one-sentence local fix. The method, rates and scope all survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The next lemma shows the way to zero out the contiguous tokens in the embedding matrix while keep other tokens unchanged via a feed-forward network.
Then we apply the Gating Lemma \ref{Gatinglemma} to have a $\mathcal{FFN}(3)$ to subtract off the constant $M$ only from columns $D+1$ to $2D$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Gating Lemma only states that an FFN keeps tokens t<=k and zeroes the data rows of all tokens t>k. In every arithmetic lemma the proof needs a different map. The offset M (or DM) must be subtracted from exactly one column, or from the window of columns D+1..2D. The tokens before the window must stay unchanged, and the zero tokens after it must remain zero. A prefix-zeroing FFN cannot do this: with k=D it erases the computed values, and with k>=2D it removes nothing. The stated lemma neither provides the needed window-selective subtraction nor a weight bound for it. All the elementary operations (sum, add, scale, square, product, power, division) rely on this step.

failure_location.quote: Then we apply the Gating Lemma \ref{Gatinglemma} to have a $\mathcal{FFN}(3)$ to subtract off the constant $DM$ in the $D+1$-th column.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove a window-gating lemma. It should give an FFN that subtracts a prescribed constant from the data row of columns in a prescribed interval and acts as the identity elsewhere. It would use the positional encodings I_t, in the same spirit as the cited Gating Lemma, with a weight bound of the same order. Then re-cite it in the arithmetic lemmas.
issues.overall_effect: The exactness of the basic arithmetic blocks, and hence of the transformer constructions for eta_i and f-hat, is not established by the cited lemmas. The weight bounds that feed kappa and the covering-number estimate are also unsupported.
issues.title: Gating Lemma used for an operation it does not provide (selective constant subtraction on a column window)
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a new but contained lemma modelled on the existing one. The architecture, rates and claims are not lost, but the fix is more than a local edit.

issues.failure_explanation: The class T(...,R,kappa) requires |T(x)| <= R for all x in R^D. The proof only controls |T-f| <= epsilon on M(q). Since |f| <= R, this gives |T| <= R+epsilon at best, even on M(q). Off M(q) there is no control: the truncated series c*sum(1-c*||eta~||_1)^k can be evaluated where ||eta~||_1 exceeds the range on which |1-c*||eta~||_1| < 1 was ensured, and the weights g(z_i) multiply it. So membership of the constructed network in the stated class is not established. The bias step in Theorem 2 and the use of the covering and oracle inequality (which need outputs bounded by R) rely on this membership.

failure_location.quote: there exists a transformer network ${\rm T}(\theta;\cdot)\in\mathcal{T}(L_{\rm T}, m_{\rm T},d_{embed},\ell,L_{\rm FFN},w_{\rm FFN},R,\kappa)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Append a final clipping layer (two ReLU units or an FFN) that truncates the output to [-R,R], or enlarge the class bound to R+1 and clip. Since |f|<=R on M(q), clipping does not increase the error on M(q) and gives a global bound.
issues.overall_effect: The existence claim in Theorem 1 is stated for a class that the constructed network may not belong to. The bias bound inf_T ||T-f||^2 <= O(eps^2) in Theorem 2, and the applicability of the oracle inequality with the R-bounded class, are therefore not rigorously justified.
issues.title: Constructed network is not shown to satisfy the class's global output bound ||T||_{L^infty(R^D)} <= R
issues.why_classification: A routine one-layer modification restores the class membership with the same orders of L_T, m_T, ell and kappa, so all claims survive.
